observations:
The gap concepts identified (שיחת חולין, פסולת ארץ ישראל, ארץ ישראל, נגב) all cluster naturally into the existing Package 1 (ארץ/נפש/דבור/צדיק). They do not form an independent domain — they are all bechina-equivalent expressions of the same dibur/nefesh/eretz nature of the Tzaddik. No three or more gap concepts point to a genuinely new domain that is structurally independent of the two packages already identified.

Specifically:
- שיחת חולין and פסולת ארץ ישראל and נגב are bechina-equivalents of one another and of ארץ/נפש/דבור — they are the 'outer husk' face of the same cluster. They do not form a separate package with its own distinct essential nature; they are sub-bechinas of Package 1.
- The ארץ ישראל composite concept is the 'holy inner' face of ארץ/נפש/דבור in the same Package 1 cluster.
- There is no evil/mirror package in this Torah at the structural level. The 'distant masses' (המון עם) and their remoteness from daat are mentioned as the cause-and-effect context (eitza), not as a bechina cluster of evil concepts. The Torah does not develop a parallel evil cluster with multiple bechina-linked concepts; it simply asserts the gap between the masses and daat as the problem the Tzaddik's speech bridges.
- The Torah has a clean two-package structure: (1) the Tzaddik-speech-soul-earth domain, (2) the daat-mountain-temple domain. The narrative is about how Package 1 bridges to Package 2 through the Tzaddik's speech acts. No third independent conceptual cluster with 3+ bechina-linked concepts emerges from this teaching.
